title: Source synthesis primitives (v1)
description: Shared primitives for the two derived synthesis records of T-251: the per-run source brief and the cross-source relation. Self-contained on purpose — these are pipeline contracts, and schemas/v1/ describes nothing the pipeline writes, so a reference into it would run the dependency backwards. The identifier patterns therefore mirror src/x2knwldg/ids.py the way schemas/v1/common.schema.json does, and tests/test_source_map_schemas.py fails the moment one of them disagrees.

schemaVersion.description: The record model version. The version is the directory: a breaking change becomes schemas/synthesis/v2/.

sourceId.$comment: ids.SourceId — '<source-type>:<external-id>'. Two parts, never three: this addresses a source, not an entity inside one.

knowledgeUnitId.$comment: The unit's canonical local id inside its own run — 'KU-000001', 'KU-D-0001'. Local, not global: a brief belongs to one source and a basis entry names its endpoint separately, so repeating the source type in every id would be a second spelling of a fact already stated.

sourceRelationId.$comment: ids.source_relation_id — 'SR-' and 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 over the endpoints, the type and the scope. A pattern check is a shape check: only recomputing the digest proves the id belongs to the record, which is the apply gate's job (T-253).

sourceRelationType.description: The eight source-to-source relation types. Mirrors constants.SOURCE_RELATION_TYPES, and deliberately not constants.RELATION_TYPES: that vocabulary joins two knowledge units, this one joins two whole sources, and 'supports' means a different-sized claim in each (risk R27).

sourceRelationScope.description: How much of the two sources the basis supports. Two values and no third: scope qualifies the claim, it does not measure it, and a percentage would be a number nothing produced (D-247).

knowledgeRelationType.description: The KU-level canonical vocabulary, mirroring constants.RELATION_TYPES. A basis entry states how one unit relates to another; the source-level type is the aggregation over those, and the two vocabularies stay apart.

runStatus.description: The status of the run a brief accounts for. UNKNOWN is absent on purpose: a brief is generated after extraction and coverage, so a run whose validators never ran has nothing to summarise, and 'UNKNOWN' here would be a brief claiming a run state nobody measured.

isoTimestamp.$comment: RFC 3339 with a required offset, exactly as schemas/v1/common.schema.json states it: a naive local time is not a point in time.

narrativeText.description: A Persian narrative statement, under the permanent output-language policy. The schema can require that text exists and is not empty; it cannot check which language it is in, so the policy is enforced by the apply gate (T-252) and by tests/test_output_language_policy.py, and this description is where the requirement is recorded rather than left implicit.

supportList.description: The knowledge units a narrative statement rests on. Non-empty, always: an empty list asserts derived knowledge while showing no work, which is exactly what adapters.base._derived_refs refuses one layer down.
